paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : MMLU Pro confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy for different accuracy metrics following model fine-tuning. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” displays a linear scale ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, with tick intervals of 0.01 representing confidence levels. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” also employs a linear scale, extending from 0.60 to 1.00 with tick intervals of 0.01 representing accuracy values. A solid blue line represents the “Final Accuracy” data, beginning at approximately 0.83 and exhibiting a generally increasing trend, reaching a value of approximately 0.96 near the end of the x-axis. A yellow line with plus signs indicates the “Δ Accuracy” data, visualized as a dashed line starting at approximately 0.30 and declining to a minimum value of approximately 0.23, then exhibiting a moderate increase to approximately 0.76. Finally, a green line with triangle markers represents the “Initial Accuracy” data, presented as a dotted line beginning at approximately 0.58 and steadily decreasing to a value of approximately 0.52 along the x-axis.
